newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Western Tanzania braces for new refugee influx.
newsitem.headline: Western Tanzania braces for new refugee influx.

text.p: Aid workers in western Tanzania expect thousands more refugees to flee Zaire by lake and land, joining more than 22,000 who have already crossed the border, the U.N. refugee agency said on Tuesday.
It also quoted refugees as saying Tutsi rebels had recently launched a new offensive southwards in eastern Zaire.

"Unless the situation in eastern Zaire improves, chances are that the current rate of influx will continue at an ever increasing rate," said a report by the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR).
It said an average of 2,000 were arriving each day across Lake Tanganyika and others by land routes so new sites had to be found to end congestion at temporary centres in Kigoma region.
UNHCR said as of Sunday a total of 22,219 refugees, most of them Zaireans but also including Burundian and Rwandan Hutus, had been registered in the Kigoma region.

"There are several thousand refugees who have also arrived in Tanzanian villages along Lake Tanganyika who have not yet been registered," said UNHCR, adding boats were scouring the shores of the lake for refugees and would bring them to Kigoma.
It said increasing numbers were likely to arrive because of fears of a fresh offensive southwards by Tutsi rebels in Zaire.
"The Banyamulenges (Tutsis) are reported to be heading towards the south in their quest for more territorial control," said the agency, citing reports from refugees.
Six members of Burundi's parliament were listed as being among the refugees.
UNHCR said except for two large boats most refugees arrived in small fishing boats with a capacity of about 100 people each.
It quoted refugees as saying boat owners had raised the price for a lake crossing from $3 to $25 per person from Fizi region in Zaire and up to $100 from the Zairean port of Kalemie.
It said new arrivals were housed in two overcrowded sites in Kigoma town -- an interior ministry compound and a stadium.
The report said there was so far no sign of malnutrition.
Before the influx from Zaire, Tanzania had some 112,000 Burundian refugees and nearly 700,000 Rwandan refugees.
